rules.body_markdown: Every game piece has an owner. Every game piece in play also has a controller.
rules.title: Every game piece has an owner.

rules.body_markdown: You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.). You’re the “owner” of these pieces.
rules.title: You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.).

rules.title: Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.

rules.body_markdown:
If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.

> **EXAMPLE:** According to the rules, you can’t attack a ready Unit, but a friendly Unit’s card text reads “This Unit can attack ready Units.” The card text overrides that rule, so the friendly Unit can declare an attack on a rival ready Unit.
rules.title: If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.

rules.body_markdown:
If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Rival plays a Unit with [ADRENALINE], which allows it to attack the turn it’s played. But a friendly Unit’s card text reads “Rival Units can't attack the turn they're played.” The preventing of the attack takes precedence, so the rival Unit can’t attack this turn.

rules.body_markdown: A game value can be a negative number.
rules.title: A game value can be a negative number.

rules.body_markdown:
When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.
rules.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

rules.body_markdown: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.
rules.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.

rules.title: A card’s “power” determines its success in stealing and fighting.

rules.title: A card’s textbox contains its card text.

rules.title: A card may have multiple textboxes.

rules.title: “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.

rules.body_markdown:
#### RAM Limits

A deck’s 3 Legends provide your deck’s “RAM Limits.” All other cards in your deck must be within these RAM Limits.
rules.title: RAM Limits

rules.body_markdown: By default, decks have a RAM Limit of 0 in all colors (0 Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).
rules.title: By default, decks have a RAM Limit of 0 in all colors (0 Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).

rules.body_markdown: When you add a Legend to your deck, increase the deck’s RAM Limits by the Legend’s RAM value.
rules.title: When you add a Legend to your deck, increase the deck’s RAM Limits by the Legend’s RAM value.

rules.body_markdown:
A deck’s RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends’ RAM in that color.

> **EXAMPLE:** A deck with “Goro Takemura: Hands Unclean” (2 Green RAM), “Saburo Arasaka: Stubborn Patriarch” (2 Green RAM), and “Yorinobu Arasaka: Embracing Destruction” (2 Red RAM), has a RAM Limit of (2 Red, 4 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).
rules.title: A deck’s RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends’ RAM in that color.

rules.body_markdown: Your deck may include any card with RAM less than or equal to your deck’s RAM Limit for its color.
rules.title: Your deck may include any card with RAM less than or equal to your deck’s RAM Limit for its color.

rules.body_markdown: Your deck’s RAM Limits are locked after deck composition. If a Legend is removed from the game during play, your deck’s RAM Limits are not affected.
rules.title: Your deck’s RAM Limits are locked after deck composition.

rules.body_markdown: RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it’s legal to include in your deck.
rules.title: RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it’s legal to include in your deck.

rules.title: Type

rules.body_markdown: A card’s type designates it as a Legend, Unit, Gear, or Program. See [CARD TYPES](#rule-8f5f8271-4cf5-5f9a-9c92-a76084ed6eed).
rules.title: A card’s type designates it as a Legend, Unit, Gear, or Program.
CARD TYPES

rules.body_markdown: The card types in *Cyberpunk TCG* are Legends, Units, Gears, and Programs.
rules.title: The card types in Cyberpunk TCG are Legends, Units, Gears, and Programs.

rules.body_markdown: A card can be multiple types simultaneously.
rules.title: A card can be multiple types simultaneously.

rules.body_markdown: Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.
rules.title: Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.

rules.body_markdown: All 3 of your Legends begin face-down in your Legends area in a random order. See [GAME SETUP](#rule-549d0f31-0614-58c3-9646-2a5c13ff4adb) > [Pre-Game Setup](#rule-5c6c550b-a5b9-5c34-8de0-ac69293d358f).
rules.title: All 3 of your Legends begin face-down in your Legends area in a random order.

rules.body_markdown: Once per turn, you may Call a Legend to flip a Legend face-up. See {[TERMS > Game Actions > Call a Legend](#rule-5a78278b-9f8b-5e64-b9aa-b2936f705af9)}.
rules.title: Once per turn, you may Call a Legend to flip a Legend face-up.

rules.body_markdown: A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area. All other areas (trash, hand, deck, etc.) are invalid areas.
rules.title: A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area.

rules.body_markdown: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.
rules.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.

rules.body_markdown: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending. Remove the Legend from the game before you resolve them. See {[GAME AREAS > Removed from Game](#rule-52d7f22c-807b-552f-afa9-bfd16bff8103)}.
rules.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending.

rules.body_markdown: You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.
rules.title: You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.

rules.body_markdown: A Legend played in this way enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area.
rules.title: A Legend played in this way enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area.

rules.title: A Legend played in this way enters with Lag.

rules.title: Legends with cost Null ( - ) do not have a cost, and cannot be played to the field.

rules.body_markdown: To play a Unit, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and place it ready in the field area.
rules.title: To play a Unit, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and place it ready in the field area.

rules.body_markdown: Units enter the field with Lag. See [Lag](#rule-6a4b19b9-eb52-5c00-af79-61a40eb948ca).
rules.title: Units enter the field with Lag.

rules.title: You may spend a Unit to declare an attack on a valid attack target.

rules.body_markdown: Gear cards can be equipped to your Units and Legends to grant them additional power and/or effects.
rules.title: Gear cards can be equipped to your Units and Legends to grant them additional power and/or effects.

rules.body_markdown: To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend. See [Equip](#rule-b076fca2-f099-5c4d-b80a-d789a90e2ce9).
rules.title: To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

rules.body_markdown: By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
rules.title: By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

rules.body_markdown: You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.
rules.title: You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.

rules.body_markdown: There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.
rules.title: There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.

rules.title: Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”

rules.body_markdown: The top textbox contains effects for the Gear. These effects are relevant when you play the Gear, and generally not relevant after a Gear is equipped.
rules.title: The top textbox contains effects for the Gear.

rules.body_markdown:
Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Gear’s top text box contains the reminder text “*(Equip to a friendly Unit or face-up Legend.)*” You equip this Gear to a friendly Unit. That Gear cannot be equipped to another friendly Unit, nor face-up Legend.

rules.title: The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to.

rules.body_markdown: Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the Gear itself.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.

rules.body_markdown: When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.
rules.title: When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

rules.body_markdown:
When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

rules.body_markdown: A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.
rules.title: A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.

rules.body_markdown: There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.
rules.title: There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.

rules.body_markdown: ### Trash Area
rules.title: Trash Area

rules.body_markdown: The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).
rules.title: The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).

rules.body_markdown: The trash is a public area.
rules.title: The trash is a public area.

rules.body_markdown: Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these cards.
rules.title: Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these ca…

rules.body_markdown: When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.
rules.title: When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.

rules.body_markdown: If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.
rules.title: If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.

rules.body_markdown: Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash. The cards in the trash should always remain in the face-up position unless specified otherwise.
rules.title: Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash.

rules.body_markdown: ### Removed from Game
rules.title: Removed from Game

rules.body_markdown: Cards removed from the game are public, and either player can freely view this area and order.
rules.title: Cards removed from the game are public, and either player can freely view this area and order.

rules.body_markdown: Cards removed from the game do not have a designated game area, because they are no longer part of the game.
rules.title: Cards removed from the game do not have a designated game area, because they are no longer part of the game.

rules.body_markdown: When a card you own is removed from the game, designate a “removed” pile outside of the game areas. Place any removed cards that you own face-up in this pile. This pile can be anywhere, as long as it is clearly visible to both players and doesn’t cause confusion with any game areas.
rules.title: When a card you own is removed from the game, designate a “removed” pile outside of the game areas.

rules.body_markdown: A card removed from the game cannot re-enter the game area unless an effect specifically returns the card to the game.
rules.title: A card removed from the game cannot re-enter the game area unless an effect specifically returns the card to the game.

rules.body_markdown: A legal deck of *Cyberpunk TCG* cards contains 3 Legend cards and a “main deck” of 40-50 non-Legend cards.
rules.title: A legal deck of Cyberpunk TCG cards contains 3 Legend cards and a “main deck” of 40-50 non-Legend cards.

rules.body_markdown:
You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name. See [Name](#rule-b311e5d2-a624-5770-a2fa-86d1db7faf78).

> **EXAMPLE:** The Legends “V: Corporate Exile” and “V: Streetkid” are both named “V,” so you can’t use both of them in the same deck.
rules.title: You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name.

rules.body_markdown: Your main deck must contain no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards.
rules.title: Your main deck must contain no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards.

rules.body_markdown: Your main deck cannot include more than three (3) copies of a card with an identical name and subtitle combination (even if they have different card numbers).
rules.title: Your main deck cannot include more than three (3) copies of a card with an identical name and subtitle combination (e…

rules.body_markdown: Your main deck may only include cards within its RAM Limits. See [RAM & Color](#rule-0667d8bc-c614-55a5-bd7d-ac8f7c6ab606).
rules.title: Your main deck may only include cards within its RAM Limits.

rules.body_markdown: If a card’s effect includes a restriction or exception to these deck requirements, your deck must adhere to that effect.
rules.title: If a card’s effect includes a restriction or exception to these deck requirements, your deck must adhere to that effect.

rules.body_markdown: All cards must be legal according to the current regulations for the game format.
rules.title: All cards must be legal according to the current regulations for the game format.

rules.body_markdown: Card sleeves must follow current regulations for the game format.
rules.title: Card sleeves must follow current regulations for the game format.

rules.body_markdown: When your turn starts, your Start Phase begins immediately. You must take these actions in this order.
rules.title: When your turn starts, your Start Phase begins immediately.

rules.body_markdown: Check if you control 7 Gig Dice. See [GAME OVERVIEW](#rule-0ef7599d-d21e-5efb-bb17-375f7950991c) > [Win Conditions](#rule-8008d6a4-9033-5412-931f-d669c00fade1).
rules.title: Check if you control 7 Gig Dice.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve any start of turn effects.
rules.title: Resolve any start of turn effects.

rules.body_markdown: Remove effects that end “at the start of your next turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Remove effects that end “at the start of your next turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve effects that occur “at the start of your turn,” “at the start of each turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Resolve effects that occur “at the start of your turn,” “at the start of each turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: Ready all spent cards in your Legends area, Field, and Eddies area.
rules.title: Ready all spent cards in your Legends area, Field, and Eddies area.

rules.body_markdown: Draw 1. (Add one card from the top of your deck to your hand.)
rules.title: Draw 1.

rules.body_markdown: If there are no cards in this area when you attempt to draw, you lose immediately. See [GAME OVERVIEW](#rule-0ef7599d-d21e-5efb-bb17-375f7950991c) > [Lose Conditions](#rule-6102756a-cd45-50fb-8ded-eea683b79df7).
rules.title: If there are no cards in this area when you attempt to draw, you lose immediately.

rules.body_markdown: “Roll in” a Gig from your fixer area.
rules.title: “Roll in” a Gig from your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: Choose a Gig from your fixer area.
rules.title: Choose a Gig from your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: You may only choose the d20 if there are no other Gigs in your fixer area.
rules.title: You may only choose the d20 if there are no other Gigs in your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: Roll the chosen Gig. The top face when it stops rolling is its value.
rules.title: Roll the chosen Gig.

rules.body_markdown: Place the Gig in the friendly Gig area, preserving the rolled value.
rules.title: Place the Gig in the friendly Gig area, preserving the rolled value.

rules.body_markdown:
### Call a Legend

As an action during your Main phase, you may spend 1 €$ to Call a Legend. See [Call a Legend](#rule-5a78278b-9f8b-5e64-b9aa-b2936f705af9).
rules.title: Call a Legend

rules.body_markdown: You may only take the “Call a Legend” game action once per turn.
rules.title: You may only take the “Call a Legend” game action once per turn.

rules.body_markdown: You may also “Call a Legend” during the React Step during your Rival’s turn.
rules.title: You may also “Call a Legend” during the React Step during your Rival’s turn.

rules.body_markdown:
### Attack

As an action during your Main phase, you may attack with a Unit. For the full rules on attacking, see [ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL](#rule-2a2dba05-9f3d-5e54-a3ec-495c89b148e1).
rules.title: Attack

rules.body_markdown: When your turn ends, you must resolve any end of turn effects in this order.
rules.title: When your turn ends, you must resolve any end of turn effects in this order.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve effects that occur “at the end of your turn,” “at the end of each turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Resolve effects that occur “at the end of your turn,” “at the end of each turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: Remove effects that last “this turn” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Remove effects that last “this turn” and variations thereof.
ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL

rules.body_markdown: “Attack” is a game action in which you spend a friendly ready Unit to attack a valid target, which results in the friendly Unit fighting or stealing.
rules.title: “Attack” is a game action in which you spend a friendly ready Unit to attack a valid target, which results in the fri…

rules.body_markdown: You may attack as a Main Phase action. See [TURN ORDER](#rule-a3a2dfd1-0994-5217-b99d-509608fc3b2e) > [Main Phase](#rule-6b35d117-68b9-5655-992b-d642e8de476d).
rules.title: You may attack as a Main Phase action.

rules.body_markdown: To attack, you must declare the attack by completing these steps in order.
rules.title: To attack, you must declare the attack by completing these steps in order.

rules.body_markdown: Choose a friendly ready Unit in the field area that can attack.
rules.title: Choose a friendly ready Unit in the field area that can attack.

rules.body_markdown: Lagging Units can’t attack. See [Lag](#rule-6a4b19b9-eb52-5c00-af79-61a40eb948ca).
rules.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.

rules.body_markdown: Choose a valid attack target for that Unit.
rules.title: Choose a valid attack target for that Unit.

rules.body_markdown: A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target.
rules.title: A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target.

rules.body_markdown: A rival Gig area containing one or more Gigs is a valid attack target. (An empty Gig area is not a valid attack target.)
rules.title: A rival Gig area containing one or more Gigs is a valid attack target.

rules.body_markdown: Card effects may add to, remove, or restrict a Unit’s valid attack targets.
rules.title: Card effects may add to, remove, or restrict a Unit’s valid attack targets.

rules.body_markdown: An effect that allows a Unit to attack only grants the specific permission described by that effect and does not remove other attack restrictions.
rules.title: An effect that allows a Unit to attack only grants the specific permission described by that effect and does not remo…

rules.body_markdown: If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack.
rules.title: If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack.

rules.body_markdown: Spend the friendly Unit.
rules.title: Spend the friendly Unit.

rules.body_markdown: Communicate the attack and the attack target to your Rival.
rules.title: Communicate the attack and the attack target to your Rival.

rules.body_markdown: When you declare an attack to your Rival, the game process of “attacking” begins immediately.
rules.title: When you declare an attack to your Rival, the game process of “attacking” begins immediately.

rules.body_markdown: While attacking, you are the “attacking player.”
rules.title: While attacking, you are the “attacking player.”

rules.body_markdown: While you’re attacking, your Rival is the “defending player.”
rules.title: While you’re attacking, your Rival is the “defending player.”

rules.body_markdown: The Unit you spend to attack is the “attacker” or “attacking Unit.” It attacks the selected target.
rules.title: The Unit you spend to attack is the “attacker” or “attacking Unit.” It attacks the selected target.

rules.body_markdown: If your attack target is a Unit, it’s called the “defending Unit,” “defender,” or “opposing Unit.”
rules.title: If your attack target is a Unit, it’s called the “defending Unit,” “defender,” or “opposing Unit.”

rules.body_markdown: If your attack target is the rival Gig area, it’s called the “defending Gig area.”
rules.title: If your attack target is the rival Gig area, it’s called the “defending Gig area.”

rules.body_markdown: When you declare the attack to your Rival, apply effects that last “while attacking” and variations thereof. All effects triggered by attacking or spending the attacker become pending. See [EFFECTS](#rule-3efdf554-b6f9-5c20-837e-5146363dd5ed) > [Pending Resolution](#rule-9afed67a-613b-547b-bbc7-75c55ca75d57)}.
rules.title: When you declare the attack to your Rival, apply effects that last “while attacking” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: After all pending effects are resolved, if the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See [ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL](#rule-2a2dba05-9f3d-5e54-a3ec-495c89b148e1) > {[Ending an Attack](#rule-ea5b950d-f8e1-5b3d-8cd5-20dec6ef700a)}. Otherwise, the attack continues; proceed to the React Step.
rules.title: After all pending effects are resolved, if the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the att…

rules.body_markdown: During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react. They may take as many reactions as they want, in any order they choose.
rules.title: During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react.

rules.body_markdown: You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.
rules.title: You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.

rules.body_markdown: You may Call a Legend as a reaction. See [Call a Legend](#rule-5a78278b-9f8b-5e64-b9aa-b2936f705af9).
rules.title: You may Call a Legend as a reaction.

rules.body_markdown: You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.
rules.title: You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.

rules.body_markdown: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.
rules.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.

rules.body_markdown: You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction. See {[TERMS > Effect Keywords > QUICK](#rule-86f65009-eda8-56d8-bc0d-58faa877bea9)}.
rules.title: You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction.

rules.body_markdown: If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.
rules.title: If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.

rules.body_markdown: If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before the defending player may take another reaction. See [EFFECTS](#rule-3efdf554-b6f9-5c20-837e-5146363dd5ed) > {[Triggered Effects](#rule-9afed67a-613b-547b-bbc7-75c55ca75d57)}.
rules.title: If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending.

rules.body_markdown: At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, the defending player may choose to end the React Step.
rules.title: At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, th…

rules.body_markdown: If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See [ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL](#rule-2a2dba05-9f3d-5e54-a3ec-495c89b148e1) > {[Ending an Attack](#rule-ea5b950d-f8e1-5b3d-8cd5-20dec6ef700a)}.
rules.title: If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends.

rules.body_markdown: When the React Step ends, the attack continues. If the attack target is a Unit, proceed to the Fight Step. If the attack target is a Gig area, proceed to the Steal Step.
rules.title: When the React Step ends, the attack continues.

rules.body_markdown: The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit. If the attack target is a Gig Area, the Steal Step happens instead.
rules.title: The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit.

rules.body_markdown: During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.
rules.title: During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.

rules.body_markdown: At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.
rules.title: At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially one winner.
rules.title: A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially…

rules.body_markdown: A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.
rules.title: A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.

rules.body_markdown: When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.
rules.title: When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.

rules.body_markdown: A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.
rules.title: A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.

rules.body_markdown: If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.
rules.title: If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.

rules.body_markdown: If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power comparison.
rules.title: If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power com…

rules.body_markdown: When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e. “when this Unit fights,” “when this Unit loses a fight,” etc.) become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before they may defeat the loser(s).
rules.title: When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e.

rules.body_markdown: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.
rules.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.

rules.body_markdown: When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.
rules.title: When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.

rules.body_markdown: When a Unit is defeated, its owner moves it to their trash.
rules.title: When a Unit is defeated, its owner moves it to their trash.

rules.body_markdown: A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.
rules.title: A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.

rules.body_markdown: If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ignores the resulting defeat.
rules.title: If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ign…

rules.body_markdown: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends. See [ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL](#rule-2a2dba05-9f3d-5e54-a3ec-495c89b148e1) > [Ending an Attack](#rule-ea5b950d-f8e1-5b3d-8cd5-20dec6ef700a).
rules.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends.

rules.body_markdown: The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area. If the attack target is a Unit, the Fight Step happens instead.
rules.title: The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area.

rules.body_markdown: If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.
rules.title: If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.

rules.body_markdown: During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.
rules.title: During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.

rules.body_markdown: At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and variations thereof. Apply any other effects that modify, prevent, or restrict the attacker’s power or ability to steal.
rules.title: At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and v…

rules.body_markdown: The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.
rules.title: The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.

rules.body_markdown: If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.
rules.title: If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.

rules.body_markdown:
If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the attacking Unit’s power.

`X = (P / 10) + 1)`

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit with 1 to 9 power steals 1 Gig. A Unit with 10 to 19 power steals 2 Gigs. Continue this pattern for higher power values.
rules.title: If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the a…

rules.body_markdown: The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.
rules.title: The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.

rules.body_markdown: An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.
rules.title: An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.

rules.body_markdown: If the attacker will steal multiple Gigs, the attacking player chooses the Gigs one at a time.
rules.title: If the attacker will steal multiple Gigs, the attacking player chooses the Gigs one at a time.

rules.body_markdown: If the attacker steals more Gigs than are in the attacked Gig area, choose as many Gigs as possible to steal.
rules.title: If the attacker steals more Gigs than are in the attacked Gig area, choose as many Gigs as possible to steal.

rules.body_markdown: After all Gigs are chosen, apply any effects that prevent or restrict one or more of those Gigs from being stolen.
rules.title: After all Gigs are chosen, apply any effects that prevent or restrict one or more of those Gigs from being stolen.

rules.body_markdown: After all Gigs are chosen and prevention effects are applied, the attacker steals the Gig(s).
rules.title: After all Gigs are chosen and prevention effects are applied, the attacker steals the Gig(s).

rules.body_markdown: To steal the Gig(s), move all chosen Gigs from the defending Gig area to the attacking Gig area at the same time.
rules.title: To steal the Gig(s), move all chosen Gigs from the defending Gig area to the attacking Gig area at the same time.

rules.body_markdown: Multiple Gigs are stolen at the same time, each stolen Gig is considered a separate stolen Gig.
rules.title: Multiple Gigs are stolen at the same time, each stolen Gig is considered a separate stolen Gig.

rules.body_markdown: Effects that trigger when a Gig is stolen become pending after a stolen Gig is moved.
rules.title: Effects that trigger when a Gig is stolen become pending after a stolen Gig is moved.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve all pending effects. See [EFFECTS](#rule-3efdf554-b6f9-5c20-837e-5146363dd5ed) > [Pending Resolution](#rule-9afed67a-613b-547b-bbc7-75c55ca75d57).
rules.title: Resolve all pending effects.

rules.body_markdown: After all pending effects from the Steal Step are resolved, the attack ends. See {[Ending an Attack](#rule-ea5b950d-f8e1-5b3d-8cd5-20dec6ef700a)}.
rules.title: After all pending effects from the Steal Step are resolved, the attack ends.

rules.body_markdown: An attack ends if any of the following are true:
rules.title: An attack ends if any of the following are true:

rules.body_markdown: The attacking Unit is no longer in the field area.
rules.title: The attacking Unit is no longer in the field area.

rules.body_markdown: The attack target is no longer in the area it was attacked in.
rules.title: The attack target is no longer in the area it was attacked in.

rules.body_markdown: The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.
rules.title: The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.

rules.body_markdown: An effect has ended the attack.
rules.title: An effect has ended the attack.

rules.body_markdown: An attack can end before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step.
rules.title: An attack can end before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step.

rules.body_markdown: If an attack ends before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step, no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen.
rules.title: If an attack ends before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step, no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen.

rules.body_markdown: If an attack ends while an effect or pending effect is resolving, finish resolving that effect or pending effect.
rules.title: If an attack ends while an effect or pending effect is resolving, finish resolving that effect or pending effect.

rules.body_markdown: When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.
rules.title: When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.

rules.body_markdown: After an attack ends and all effects and pending effects for the current timing window have resolved, remove effects that last “while attacking,” “while stealing,” “while fighting” and variations thereof. The turn player’s Main Phase continues.
rules.title: After an attack ends and all effects and pending effects for the current timing window have resolved, remove effects…
EFFECTS

rules.body_markdown: An effect is card text that affects the game. Card text is the source of effects.
rules.title: An effect is card text that affects the game.

rules.body_markdown: Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.
rules.title: Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.

rules.body_markdown: Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.
rules.title: Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.

rules.body_markdown: When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers to the source of that effect unless another rule or effect says otherwise.
rules.title: When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers t…

rules.body_markdown: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect. You are the one who resolves it.
rules.title: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect.

rules.body_markdown: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.
rules.title: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.

rules.body_markdown: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See [GOLDEN RULES](#rule-68b314b6-4bba-5507-b8f0-929a8baff26d) > [Resolve as Much as Possible](#rule-a1137877-3824-5786-bc49-9ca22d5054ba).
rules.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.

rules.body_markdown: If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed by their Rival.
rules.title: If an effect instructs both players to act at the same time, the turn player performs their actions first, followed b…

rules.body_markdown: Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the current effect finishes resolving.
rules.title: Once an effect starts resolving, you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the…

rules.body_markdown: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects. If an effect triggers in the middle of an activation or resolution, it becomes “pending resolution.” See [EFFECTS](#rule-3efdf554-b6f9-5c20-837e-5146363dd5ed) > [Pending Resolution](#rule-9afed67a-613b-547b-bbc7-75c55ca75d57).
rules.title: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects.

rules.body_markdown: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
rules.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

rules.body_markdown: An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)
rules.title: An effect may include conditions.

rules.body_markdown: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
rules.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

rules.body_markdown: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See [Cost](#rule-a2a83a05-cee0-530e-beb1-b3b588453fa6).
rules.title: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost.

rules.body_markdown: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
rules.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

rules.body_markdown: There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.
rules.title: There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.

rules.body_markdown: A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.
rules.title: A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.

rules.body_markdown: You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.
rules.title: You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.

rules.body_markdown: A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.
rules.title: A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.

rules.body_markdown: A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.
rules.title: A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.

rules.body_markdown: An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.
rules.title: An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.

rules.body_markdown: An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.
rules.title: An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.

rules.body_markdown: If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.
rules.title: If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.

rules.body_markdown: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
rules.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

rules.body_markdown: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.
rules.title: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

rules.body_markdown: If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid and the controlling player does not make a choice.

rules.body_markdown: If an activated effect has additional activation conditions that are invalid, you cannot activate the effect.
rules.title: If an activated effect has additional activation conditions that are invalid, you cannot activate the effect.

rules.body_markdown: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.
rules.title: If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

rules.body_markdown: If resolving a pending effect requires information about a game piece that is no longer valid, use the information from when the piece was last valid.

rules.body_markdown: A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.
rules.title: A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.

rules.body_markdown: You cannot take any game actions until all pending effects are resolved.
rules.title: You cannot take any game actions until all pending effects are resolved.

rules.body_markdown: Once an effect becomes pending, it remains pending until it resolves or a rule or effect removes it from pending.
rules.title: Once an effect becomes pending, it remains pending until it resolves or a rule or effect removes it from pending.

rules.body_markdown: After a pending effect resolves, it stops being pending.
rules.title: After a pending effect resolves, it stops being pending.

rules.body_markdown: If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.
rules.title: If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.

rules.body_markdown: If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before their Rival resolves all of theirs.

rules.body_markdown: If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too. Finish resolving the current pending effect before resolving any new pending effects.
rules.title: If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too.

rules.body_markdown: If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending effects finishes resolving all of their pending effects (including the new ones) before their Rival resolves their new ones.

rules.body_markdown: Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution).
rules.title: Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect…

rules.body_markdown: If a pending effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution, that condition must still be true when the effect resolves.

rules.body_markdown: A triggered effect has a trigger condition.
rules.title: A triggered effect has a trigger condition.

rules.body_markdown: A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.
rules.title: A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.

rules.body_markdown: If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.
rules.title: If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.

rules.body_markdown:
If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that condition is met.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "When this Unit steals a Gig, increase it by up to 5.” In this example, the trigger is “When this Unit steals a Gig.” If the Unit steals 2 Gigs at the same time, then the effect “increase it by up to 5” becomes pending twice.

rules.title: You may activate “activated effects” as an action during your Main Phase.

When an activated effect has a colon, the bolded text preceding the colon is the activation cost, and the text following the colon is the effect that resolves after you pay the activation cost. See [Cost](#rule-a2a83a05-cee0-530e-beb1-b3b588453fa6).

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "[Spend Icon] Swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig.” This is an activated effect. During your Main Phase, you may spend the Unit as an activation cost; if you do, you gain the effect “Swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig.”

rules.title: Choices and costs before the colon are made or paid while activating the effect.

rules.body_markdown: You must pay all activation costs for an effect. If you can’t pay all required costs, you cannot activate the effect.
rules.title: You must pay all activation costs for an effect.

rules.body_markdown: If an effect has multiple activation costs, pay them in the order that they appear.
rules.title: If an effect has multiple activation costs, pay them in the order that they appear.

rules.body_markdown: Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.
rules.title: Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.

rules.body_markdown: Choose a valid friendly effect to activate. See [EFFECTS](#rule-3efdf554-b6f9-5c20-837e-5146363dd5ed) > [Valid & Invalid Effects](#rule-da178967-2dfb-5484-b475-46e3cae8bf31).
rules.title: Choose a valid friendly effect to activate.

rules.body_markdown: If the activated effect is on a card in a hidden area (like your hand), reveal it.
rules.title: If the activated effect is on a card in a hidden area (like your hand), reveal it.

rules.body_markdown: If the effect requires a choice or valid target, choose them.
rules.title: If the effect requires a choice or valid target, choose them.

rules.title: Communicate the effect and any choices/targets to your Rival.

rules.title: Resolve any pending effects.

rules.body_markdown: Once an activated effect is activated, it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in.
rules.title: Once an activated effect is activated, it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in.

rules.body_markdown: A persistent effect continuously applies while it is active.
rules.title: A persistent effect continuously applies while it is active.

rules.body_markdown: A persistent effect is not activated.
rules.title: A persistent effect is not activated.

rules.body_markdown: A persistent effect never becomes pending.
rules.title: A persistent effect never becomes pending.

rules.body_markdown: A persistent effect applies only while its source is in the area where that effect is active.
rules.title: A persistent effect applies only while its source is in the area where that effect is active.

rules.body_markdown:
If a persistent effect has a duration, it applies only for that duration.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit's effect text reads "Other friendly Units have +2 power while attacking.” The Unit only gains +2 from the moment the Unit attacks until the attack ends.
rules.title: If a persistent effect has a duration, it applies only for that duration.

rules.body_markdown: When a persistent effect’s duration ends, that effect stops applying immediately once there are no other pending effects.

A replacement effect replaces one action or process with another. (They often use “would” and “instead.”)

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit inherits the effect text from a Gear that reads "If this Unit would be defeated, defeat its "DEADMAN TRANSMITTER" instead.” The effect “defeat [this Unit’s] "DEADMAN TRANSMITTER"” replaces the game process of defeating the Unit.
rules.title: A replacement effect replaces one action or process with another.

rules.body_markdown: A replacement effect applies before (and instead of) the action or process it replaces. The replaced action or process does not occur at all.
rules.title: A replacement effect applies before (and instead of) the action or process it replaces.

rules.body_markdown: If a replacement effect is optional, the player who controls that replacement effect may choose not to apply it.

rules.body_markdown: If it’s not possible to perform the replacement, that replacement effect cannot be applied.
rules.title: If it’s not possible to perform the replacement, that replacement effect cannot be applied.

rules.body_markdown: ### Lag
rules.title: Lag

rules.body_markdown: Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field. Units with Lag are also called “lagging.”
rules.title: Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field.

rules.body_markdown: Lagging Units can’t attack.
rules.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.

rules.body_markdown: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.
rules.title: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.

rules.body_markdown: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.
rules.title: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.

rules.body_markdown: ### Equip
rules.title: Equip

rules.body_markdown: “Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it. When you do, the Gear becomes “equipped to” that card. See [CARD TYPES](#rule-8f5f8271-4cf5-5f9a-9c92-a76084ed6eed) > [Gear](#rule-0dffbbac-b466-5f3f-9f66-0ff9ef80cd49).
rules.title: “Equip” is a game action in which you attach a Gear to a Unit or Legend by placing the card beneath it.

rules.body_markdown: When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.
rules.title: When a Gear is equipped make sure only the bottom text box is showing under the equipped card.

rules.body_markdown: Gear stays equipped unless it (or the Unit/Legend it’s equipped to) is defeated or moves outside of the Legends area or field.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend with one or more Gears attached is “equipped.”

rules.body_markdown: A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”
rules.title: A Unit or Legend with no Gear attached is “unequipped.”

rules.body_markdown: Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.
rules.title: Units and Legends inherit all effects in the bottom textbox of their equipped Gears.

rules.body_markdown: Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.
rules.title: Units and Legends gain the power of their equipped Gears.

rules.body_markdown: "Move" is a game action in which you unequip a Gear from the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to and equip it to another valid Unit or Legend.

rules.body_markdown: ### Call a Legend
rules.title: Call a Legend

rules.body_markdown: “Call a Legend” is a game action in which you pay 1 €$ to flip a face-down Legend face-up.
rules.title: “Call a Legend” is a game action in which you pay 1 €$ to flip a face-down Legend face-up.

rules.body_markdown: You may choose any one (1) friendly face-down Legend in your Legends area.
rules.title: You may choose any one (1) friendly face-down Legend in your Legends area.

rules.body_markdown: A Legend flipped face-up through the Call a Legend action is a “called” Legend.
rules.title: A Legend flipped face-up through the Call a Legend action is a “called” Legend.

rules.body_markdown: The called Legend maintains its orientation (spent or ready) when flipped face-up.
rules.title: The called Legend maintains its orientation (spent or ready) when flipped face-up.

rules.body_markdown: When you flip a Legend face up this way it activates any [CALL] keyword effects on that Legend. See [\[CALL\]](#rule-d2312a93-5d92-5ea9-8931-a7ec2cf099a3).
rules.title: When you flip a Legend face up this way it activates any [CALL] keyword effects on that Legend.

rules.body_markdown: You may only Call a Legend once per turn.
rules.title: You may only Call a Legend once per turn.

rules.body_markdown: You may Call a Legend as an action during your main phase.
rules.title: You may Call a Legend as an action during your main phase.

rules.body_markdown: You may Call a Legend as a reaction when a rival Unit attacks.
rules.title: You may Call a Legend as a reaction when a rival Unit attacks.

What happens to a Gear on a Legend when the Legend is removed from play?
faqs.answer: When a Legend leaves the field or Legends area, its attached Gear follows the Legend to that area, then is no longer equipped in the new area. So, the Gear remains in that new area when you remove the Legend from play.
